The two figures side by side so the size of the uplift is visible, as the clause requires: POL-RD-02 gives 14.15; the uplifted figure is 42.05. There is no government-set or third-party pass-through line to carve out — ERP, tolls and any surcharge are all 0.00 — so the uplift is not reduced for them.

The same clause additionally requires the case to be referred to driver-conduct review. That referral is an addition to a monetary ruling, not an escalation: money still moves, and under POL-GEN-03 a referral never suppresses the refund.

The ledger carries no ERP gantry lines at all (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.0, and both the on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route gantry totals 0.00) and no airport surcharge, so there is nothing to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and nothing to double count under POL-RD-09(1): the whole contest is the distance and time the detour added, and every dollar of the rider's refund traces to a line of the fare_breakdown.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (all TRP-00306) and the pickup timestamp 22:35:20 is consistent, so trigger (2) is not engaged and trigger (4) has no disagreement of more than 10 minutes to point at; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so trigger (3) is not engaged; the POL-RD-02 refund of 14.15 is far below both SGD 150.00 and charged_total, so trigger (6) is not engaged; and the only missing artifact is an advisory no party cites by evidence ID, which POL-RD-13(1) keeps out of trigger (5). The case can be decided on this record.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: the artifacts describe the same trip on matching identifiers and pickup timestamp, and the excess is measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. The burden then shifts to the driver, who has pointed to no admissible artifact and no clause that survives POL-RD-13. The rider's own citable counters are clean — deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0 — so the corroboration uplift for repeat unsubstantiated claimants is not required of this claim; every other rider profile field is context only under POL-GEN-01 and grounds nothing.

The rider's demand for the whole fare is not what the policy's own arithmetic produces on this trip. charged_total is SGD 42.05 and recomputed_fare on the booked route is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 27.0 optimal min) x 1.0 surge, read from the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 27.91, so the POL-RD-02 refund is 42.05 - 27.91 = SGD 14.14, rounded up to SGD 14.15. That is 33.6% of the charged total, far below the 90% share at which POL-RD-02 directs a FULL_REFUND instead of a partial, and the rider did consume the full 33.5 km ride at the metered rate. The claim for the entire trip therefore exceeds anything the fare lines can support.

No charge may be stacked on top of that differential. The fare ledger carries no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge on this non-airport trip, and the 33.5 km billed distance matches the trace's own 33.48 km, so there is no phantom gantry, no wrongly applied surcharge and no unbilled distance to correct. POL-RD-09 has no standalone pass-through or billing-integrity correction to make here, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting any ERP element a second time inside the POL-RD-02 figure.

The driver's roadblock explanation cannot be run and is not pressed as an exoneration, because the bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip: EV-ADVIS-00306-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (no advisory covers the SLE or CTE in this window). As an artifact at weight 0.0 it can carry no fact, POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record, and under POL-RD-13 the assertion neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal; the deviation therefore stands at the measured figure on the booked optimal route.

No other clause moves the baseline either, so nothing may be substituted for the booked 21.0 km optimal. The chat log carries 0 messages and no waypoint, so the POL-RD-04 rider-instruction test cannot be run; the trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at null with amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 cannot apply and no amended optimal exists; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 is not in play. The POL-RD-02 computation runs on the booked optimal route and on no invented alternative.

Whatever figure issues, it does not move on issue. The monetary effect here (SGD 14.15, and a fortiori any larger figure) exceeds the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so under POL-GEN-05 the amount is held rather than executed and the case goes to the human queue for release; no automatic adjustment is made against the driver on issue.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: this is a route-deviation dispute over trip TRP-00306, Yishun MRT to Raffles Place on 8 Aug 2026, charged SGD 42.05 on a metered fare.

Rider — your account of the route is borne out by the platform's own data. The routing engine's optimal distance is 21.0 km (EV-TRIP-00306; optimal is SLE then CTE) and the GPS trace records 33.48 km driven (EV-GPS-00306). Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs and the rounded 33.5 km on the trip record may not be cited for the threshold test: the excess is 12.48 km, or 59.43% of optimal. Both establishment tests (over 0.8 km and over 20%) pass, and the excess also clears 8.0 km and 50%, so the deviation is MATERIAL. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 265 fixes, 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, empty gaps array and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 s — so the deviation may rest on the trace alone and no corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is needed.

Driver — your explanation that a police roadblock on the SLE forced you onto the BKE cannot be tested against anything. The only traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-00306-01, is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, 'No advisory covers the SLE or CTE in this window'), and you named no evidence ID for any advisory. Under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 your assertion is discarded: it neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal, and POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record. Because no party cited an advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and the case does not escalate on that ground. No other exoneration applies either: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00306) has zero messages, so the POL-RD-04 rider-instruction test cannot be run and nothing is excluded; pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null with amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 does not run; and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline is irrelevant.

Money. The fare is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 runs. charged_total is SGD 42.05. recomputed_fare is (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 km + 0.28 x 27.0 min) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee = SGD 27.91. The POL-RD-02 figure is therefore 42.05 less 27.91 = SGD 14.14, rounded up to SGD 14.15. That is the partial your submission argues for, and it is the correct figure on POL-RD-02 alone.

But that is not the end of it. The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is mandatory on a material deviation. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3, which meets the pattern test on its own limb (3 or more in the trailing 90-day window); those two counters are the only citable profile fields under POL-GEN-01, and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter of 7 is context only. This trip's deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on its own trace, so POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of the charged total rather than the POL-RD-02 partial. The two figures side by side: POL-RD-02 partial SGD 14.15; uplifted figure SGD 42.05. There are no government-set or third-party pass-through lines to carve out — ERP, tolls and any surcharge are all 0.00 on this non-airport trip — so nothing is settled separately under POL-RD-09 and nothing is double-counted under POL-RD-09(1). Your position that the whole-fare demand 'exceeds anything the fare lines can support' is therefore accepted only as to the POL-RD-02 arithmetic and is outweighed by POL-RD-06(b).

Ruling: FULL_REFUND of SGD 42.05 to the rider. Confidence is capped at 1.0 because every artifact carrying a deciding fact — the trace, the trip record, the driver profile and the fare breakdown — carries weight_multiplier 1.0; no impaired artifact carries any deciding fact.

Referral: under POL-RD-06(c) the case is referred to driver-conduct review. That referral rides with the money and does not displace or delay it.

Execution: the monetary effect exceeds the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so the amount is issued but held and the case enters the human queue for release.

Audit note: one rider claim was discarded in the mechanical pre-check — a claim about the absent advisory that cited EV-ADVIS-00306-01 at weight 0.0 without naming its issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the disclosure requirement of POL-GEN-02(1) was not met. The substance of that point is preserved by the surviving claims above.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
